CcMap.description: Bind one CC to one parameter, scaled over its range.

pickup.description: Only take over once the knob passes the current value.

Change.description:
One change to an addressable piece of project state, e.g.
`param:mixer.2.volume`, `step:drums.kick.3`, `note:bass.5`,
`instrument:bass`, `channel:2`, `channels:order`, `route:drums.kick`.
`null` means absent (or, for params and steps, the default).

device.description: Hardware currently attached as a Livid Block, if any.

focus.description:
That seat's focused instrument: the grid edits it when it is a
`tr808` (otherwise the grid is dark) and the knobs control its page.

follow.description: When true, the page follows the playhead while playing.

knob_page.description: Knob page in use (an id from `knob_pages`).

knob_params.description: Parameter path each knob currently controls. Empty without focus.

leds.description: 8 rows x 8 columns of LED values (0 = off, 1 = on).

page.description: Which 8-step page the grid shows (0 = steps 1-8, 1 = steps 9-16, ...).

seat.description: The seat the engine host's own devices (the Block) belong to.

DeviceProfile.description: How a device's input is interpreted.

oneOf.description: Notes and CCs, routed by the seat's bindings and CC maps.
Grid + knobs as a surface for the seat's focus, LEDs driven.
A note pattern changed (all `MAX_STEPS` steps).

Instruments, channels, or routes changed. Parameters may have been
added or removed: refetch `state.get` and `param.list`.
A step started. `time` is engine time in seconds.

An instrument played (from the sequencer, a pad, MIDI, or an
audition). Drums set `voice`; note instruments set `note`.

Peak levels since the last meter event (linear, 0..1+), per active
channel (post fader, pan, and mute/solo) and for the master.
Seats, their bindings, or who sits where changed.

Raw incoming MIDI, for discovering controller mappings. `port` is
the port name (for `midi.input`, the logical device name).
A user's undo/redo summary changed.
A request was recorded in the journal.
State was replaced wholesale (project load/new); refetch `state.get`.
This subscriber fell behind and missed events; refetch `state.get`.

auto_seat.description: Match a seat by `user` (default true). False stays unseated.

client_name.description: Display name for this client; used as event origin.

seat.description: Join this existing seat instead of matching by `user`.

token.description: Required when the daemon was started with `--token`.

user.description:
The person using this client: owns this connection's undo history
(default: the daemon host's user, so local clients share one). A
seat with this name (any case) is joined automatically if it is the
only match; in a project without seats, one is created for them.

channel.description:
Route the main output to this existing channel. By default it goes to
the first empty channel in display order, or a new one if none is empty.

id.description: Defaults to the type's default id (`drums`, `bass`), numbered if taken.

no_channel.description: Leave the main output unrouted (no new channel).

keep_channels.description: Keep the channels its outputs fed even if they are left empty.

value.description: Normalized position 0..1 (as from a 0..127 MIDI CC).

input.description: Input port name (exact or case-insensitive substring).

name.description:
Logical device name. Default: the saved one, else made from the port

output.description:
Output port for feedback (LEDs). Defaults to the output matching the
input for a Livid Block.

profile.description:
Default: the saved one, else `livid_block` for ports named like a
Block, else `generic`.

data.description: Raw MIDI bytes of one message, e.g. `[144, 60, 100]`.

device.description: Logical device name the input comes from.

profile.description:
How to read the bytes; default: the connected device's profile, else
generic. Input from a device on the engine host carries it, so the
journal replays it the same way where that device is not connected.

seat.description:
Seat to apply; default: the caller's, else the host seat. A Livid
Block only edits the host seat (its LEDs show that one).

substring of a port).

Seat for this machine's devices; omit to unpin (they then follow
